{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team / Business Owner  
**From:** In-house Counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement (Customer side)

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The risk-allocation core of the agreement is strong for us: indemnification (§ 20), IP and Customer Data ownership (§ 14), limitation of liability (§ 21), licence scope (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), warranties (§ 19), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), governing law (§ 28) and insurance (§ 18) all sit at or above our preferred positions and require no redlines.

Our concerns are concentrated in the commercial-commitment and administrative provisions, several of which contradict § 12.3 (in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer or no-hire commitment) and § 2.1 (no minimum or purchase commitment). Six items require change:

- **Walk-away territory (four items):** full-term sole-and-exclusive sourcing (§ 2.2), uncapped Customer-payable liquidated damages of USD 25,000 per day (§ 7.6), an open-ended Customer most-favoured-nation obligation (§ 7.2), and unlimited unannounced Vendor audits with remote access to our systems (§ 22.1). A three-year term with no Customer termination-for-convenience right (Sections 8–9) is likewise walk-away territory and is treated as a missing clause.
- **Fallback breaches:** a one-way 18-month non-solicit/no-engage covenant against us (§ 12.4) and a 180-day non-renewal notice window (§ 8.2).

We recommend pressing the exclusivity, liquidated damages, MFN, audit and termination-for-convenience points as conditions of signature, and resolving the internal conflicts with §§ 2.1 and 12.3 in the operative clauses.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 (with §§ 20.2–20.5, 21.3) | Express Vendor defend/indemnify/hold-harmless for IP claims, plus law breach, data incidents, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud; standard procedure and uncapped treatment. No redline. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (with §§ 1.4, 1.8, 13.2, 14.2–14.4, 15.1) | We own Customer Data and Deliverables (present assignment); Vendor retains only Vendor Technology, channelled into a perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence. No redline. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 1.5, 21.2–21.4, 18.2) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; mutual consequential exclusion; all required carve-outs in § 21.3. No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Free Customer assignment to Affiliate or successor on notice; Vendor assignment/change of control gated on our consent; § 24.4 closes the walk-away trigger. No redline. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 | Vendor is our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics for the full term: no category narrowing, no 12-month limit, no performance exit. Walk-away; fails every fallback element and conflicts with §§ 2.1 and 12.3. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 | Uncapped USD 25,000 per day payable by us for any delay in providing a dependency. Walk-away; per-day accrual is unbounded and can exceed remaining contract value. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.4, 24.1) | Rights extend to Affiliates, contractors and Authorized Users; paid-up licences perpetual and irrevocable; narrow restrictions; real successor-transfer path. Above fallback. No redline. |
| High | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | We must extend Vendor the best terms given any other technology supplier, with no product, time or like-for-like limits. Walk-away; contradicts § 12.3. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 (with §§ 2.1, 13.1, 13.4) | Customer's freedom to develop, acquire, licence, sell or use any product and operate in any field or territory is expressly preserved. No redline. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | §§ 8.1, 9.1–9.3 (also §§ 6.2, 19.4, 20.5, 27.3) | Three-year term with only cause-, insolvency- and Vendor-failure-based termination. No Customer convenience right anywhere; walk-away for a multi-year term. § 8.2 non-renewal is handled under RENEWAL. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 | Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems. Walk-away; fails fallback on frequency and notice and contradicts the protective language in § 22.2. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with §§ 28.2–28.3) | New York law, CISG excluded, exclusive New York County jurisdiction; no arbitration; escalation does not displace the forum. Preferred position. No redline. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2.1 (with §§ 7.1, 12.3, 22.2–22.3) | No minimum quantity, purchase commitment, take-or-pay or volume restriction; non-ordering is not a breach or shortfall. No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | One-way 18-month covenant running from termination, covering any Vendor employee during the term, barring engagement (a no-hire) with no advertising carve-out. Fails every material fallback element; contradicts § 12.3. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 8.2 (pricing at § 8.3) | Twelve-month auto-renewal with a 180-day non-renewal notice window — beyond the 60-day fallback maximum and within walk-away territory. Renewal pricing in § 8.3 already beats our position. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 (with §§ 11.2–11.3, 16.5) | Up to six months' assistance on any termination at expiring Order Form rates; machine-readable data return within 30 days of our request; certified deletion after return. No redline. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5) | Professional/workmanlike and conformance warranties; 90 days for Deliverables and the full subscription term for Hosted Services; re-perform/repair/replace, then terminate and refund. No redline. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) | CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M (unconditional), workers' compensation as required; certificates, primacy and no limitation of liability. Preferred position. No redline. |

---

## Walk-away Items

The following provisions fall into walk-away territory under our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **§ 2.2 — Full-term sole-and-exclusive sourcing.** Exclusive dealing for the entire term with no product-category narrowing, no 12-month limit and no exit for missed service levels or delivery dates. Our position is a non-exclusive appointment with express confirmation that we owe no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation, which also cures the conflict with §§ 2.1 and 12.3.
2. **§ 7.6 — Uncapped Customer-payable liquidated damages.** USD 25,000 per day for any delay in providing a dependency, triggered by even trivial delay, with no cap and no offsetting service credits. Our position is that we pay no liquidated damages or penalties; the fallback permits only an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees. No other clause cross-references § 7.6, so the edit is surgical.
3. **§ 7.2 — Open-ended Customer MFN.** No product limitation, no time limit and no like-for-like comparison carve-outs; the only MFN mechanic in the document runs against us. We propose converting § 7.2 into an express confirmation that no Customer MFN applies, consistent with § 12.3.
4. **§ 22.1 — Unlimited unannounced audits with remote system access.** Our position: one audit per 12 months on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, off-site where possible, by a confidentiality-bound independent auditor, with the remote-access grant deleted. The protective § 22.2 cost allocation (5% underpayment threshold) and no-direct-access language are retained verbatim.
5. **Sections 8–9 — No Customer termination for convenience on a three-year term.** We propose a new § 9.4 at our preferred level: 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirmation that Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term. 60 days' notice is available as a fallback.
6. **§ 8.2 — 180-day non-renewal notice window.** Windows longer than 90 days are walk-away territory. We seek the smallest change to reach the fallback: shorten to sixty (60) days.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Confirm commercial appetite** on the four walk-away commercial terms (§§ 2.2, 7.2, 7.6 and the absence of a convenience right) with the business owner before we issue the markup.
2. **Issue the redline** covering the six change items:
   - § 2.2 — convert to non-exclusive; confirm no Customer exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
   - § 7.2 — convert to an express confirmation that no Customer MFN obligation exists.
   - § 7.6 — remove the per-day liquidated damages and confirm no LDs or penalties are payable by Customer.
   - New § 9.4 — 30-day Customer convenience termination with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; no Vendor convenience right during a committed term.
   - § 12.4 — replace the Customer-only 18-month non-solicit/no-engage covenant with an express statement that Customer has no non-solicitation restriction; offer the narrow mutual 12-month fallback in the comment.
   - § 8.2 — shorten the non-renewal notice window from 180 days to sixty (60) days.
3. **Flag the internal inconsistencies** to Vendor's counsel in cover comments: §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 each contradict § 12.3, and § 22.1 contradicts § 22.2. Resolving them in the operative clauses should be presented as clean-up rather than a concession.
4. **Record the fallback landing zones** we can accept without further escalation: 60 days' notice for convenience termination, 60 days for non-renewal, and a mutual 12-month narrow non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services with a general-advertising carve-out.
5. **Note for the file (no action):** § 14.2 conditions Deliverable ownership on payment of applicable Fees and § 1.4 excludes unaided-memory know-how; the § 21 payment carve-out is limited to undisputed Fees for conforming Services; the § 19.3 malicious-code warranty is limited to code intentionally introduced by Vendor; and no Vendor renewal-reminder mechanic exists. These are noted for information only and are not being redlined."}
